authoring_rationale: Class C: persistence, engaged; Part D condition (b). One variant is unambiguous: all flagged entries are removed whatever their age, and drafts are removed once older than ninety days. The other says the tidy-up removes 'flagged entries and drafts older than ninety days', where the age limit can attach to drafts only (the same as the first variant) or to both flagged entries and drafts (recent flagged entries survive the month, which differs). Both readings are grammatical and nothing else in that variant fixes the attachment; the readings differ in what survives. Locatable at that one coordinated phrase. A substantive answer would require choosing a reading the text does not fix. Drafting note: a closing clause advising the reader to check flags before month end was removed from both variants before any bytes were built, because it weakly favoured one reading. Authored fresh from the public ADR-0054 and ADR-0055 law only; not adapted from or templated on any other case or corpus; no void-attempt material used. Orientation and identity computed mechanically from the final bytes (ADR-0055 decisions 7, 8 and 11); no wording was adjusted for orientation, identity or position.
